body:
See #8589 for socket path derivation.  This `0` suggests to me that the postgres host is configured empty or not configured, but I don't yet know how.  Running tserver with `--vmodule=tablet=1` will cause a log to show the index backfill connection string.

Also, you can look at the current tserver logs for a line like

```
I0518 14:12:30.463384 26427 tablet_server_main.cc:242] Starting PostgreSQL server listening on 127.0.0.11, port 5433
```

to show what the postgres host is set to.  In the above, it's `127.0.0.11`.

The directory not existing is unexpected, like there's some mismatch between startup and index creation time, so providing extra details would help.

I do have the socket under `/tmp`, just not under `0`. E.g. 
```
lrwxrwxrwx 1 root root   23 May 24 12:46 .yb.0 -> .yb.8228272234018189749
drwxr-xr-x 2 root root 4096 May 24 12:45 .yb.8228272234018189749
```

That's what I meant with "symlink workaround". I am running an local experimental setup with `docker-compose` almost the same as in documentation:

```
version: '2'

volumes:
  yb-master-data-1:
  yb-tserver-data-1:

networks:
  dbinternal:
  dbnet:

services:
  yb-master:
      image: yugabytedb/yugabyte:latest
      container_name: yb-master-n1
      networks:
      - dbinternal
      volumes:
      - yb-master-data-1:/mnt/master
      command: [ "/home/yugabyte/bin/yb-master",
                "--fs_data_dirs=/mnt/master",
                "--master_addresses=yb-master-n1:7100",
                "--rpc_bind_addresses=yb-master-n1:7100",
                "--replication_factor=1"]
      ports:
      - "7000:7000"
      environment:
        SERVICE_7000_NAME: yb-master

  yb-tserver:
      image: yugabytedb/yugabyte:latest
      container_name: yb-tserver-n1
      networks:
      - dbinternal
      - dbnet
      volumes:
      - yb-tserver-data-1:/mnt/tserver
      command: [ "/home/yugabyte/bin/yb-tserver",
                "--fs_data_dirs=/mnt/tserver",
                "--start_pgsql_proxy",
                "--rpc_bind_addresses=yb-tserver-n1:9100",
                "--tserver_master_addrs=yb-master-n1:7100"
                ]
      ports:
      - "9042:9042"
      - "5433:5433"
      - "9000:9000"
      environment:
        SERVICE_5433_NAME: ysql
        SERVICE_9042_NAME: ycql
        SERVICE_6379_NAME: yedis
        SERVICE_9000_NAME: yb-tserver
      depends_on:
      - yb-master
```

Experiment with `2.4` uses exactly the same configuration, just `yugabytedb/yugabyte:latest` is replaced with `yugabytedb/yugabyte:2.4.4.0-b7`.

This issue has come up about three times from some users on community Slack as well.

## repro

The combination of reports helped me create a repro (sorry I didn't follow through with the above comment):

1. Apply patch to have yb-ctl avoid specifying `pgsql_proxy_bind_address` flag:

   ```diff
   diff --git i/scripts/installation/bin/yb-ctl w/scripts/installation/bin/yb-ctl
   index dfc0ecf4b7..9e6cc098c6 100755
   --- i/scripts/installation/bin/yb-ctl
   +++ w/scripts/installation/bin/yb-ctl
   @@ -1363,8 +1363,6 @@ class ClusterControl:
            if self.is_ysql_enabled():
                command_list += [
                    "--enable_ysql=true",
   -                "--pgsql_proxy_bind_address=" +
   -                self.options.get_client_listen_host_port(daemon_id, 'ysql')
                ]
                if (self.options.ysql_hba_conf_csv is not None):
                    command_list.append(
   ```

1. Shut down anything else listening on port 5433 (since postgres will listen on 0.0.0.0:5433)
1. `yb-ctl create`
1. `ysqlsh --command 'create table t (i int)'; ysqlsh --command 'create index on t (i)'` and get

   ```
   ERROR:  Aborted: backfill connection to DB failed: could not connect to server: No such file or directory
           Is the server running locally and accepting
           connections on Unix domain socket "/tmp/.yb.0/.s.PGSQL.5433"?
   ```

## reason

If yb-tserver is run without `pgsql_proxy_bind_address` flag set, the local postgres is run with the default 0.0.0.0 listen address.  postgres derives the socket dir using "0.0.0.0" while tserver derives it using "".

```cpp
struct PgProcessConf {
  static constexpr uint16_t kDefaultPort = 5433;
  ...
  std::string listen_addresses = "0.0.0.0";
```

```cpp
  if (!bind_addresses.empty()) {
    auto pg_host_port = VERIFY_RESULT(HostPort::FromString(
        bind_addresses, PgProcessConf::kDefaultPort));
    conf.listen_addresses = pg_host_port.host();
```

postgres creates "0.0.0.0" socket dir, resulting in hash 8228272234018189749:

```cpp
  argv.push_back("-k");
  const std::string& socket_dir = PgDeriveSocketDir(conf_.listen_addresses);
```

tserver uses "" socket dir during index backfill, resulting in hash 0:

```cpp
  std::string conn_str = Format(
      "user=$0 password=$1 host=$2 port=$3 dbname=$4",
      "postgres",
      postgres_auth_key,
      PgDeriveSocketDir(pgsql_proxy_bind_address.host()),
      pgsql_proxy_bind_address.port(),
      pgwrapper::PqEscapeLiteral(database_name));
```

## fix

One fix is to treat empty string as "0.0.0.0" on tserver-side (`tablet.cc`).  Possibly a better solution is to set `tablet_server.h`'s `pgsql_proxy_bind_address_` default value to `"0.0.0.0"`.

Also, issue #8589 would have made debugging this easier.

issue.body:
Jira Link: [DB-1692](https://yugabyte.atlassian.net/browse/DB-1692)
Using YB-2.5.0.0 on macOS Big Sur Version 11.0.1.

Testcase:

```
\set VERBOSITY verbose
drop table if exists t cascade;

create table t(
  k  int primary key,
  v  int not null
  );

-- insert into t(k, v) values(1, 42);

create index t_v
on t(v);
```

It causes this outcome:

```
ERROR:  38000: index backfill failed
LOCATION:  DefineIndex, indexcmds.c:1350
```

It makes no difference if "insert into t(k, v) values(1, 42)" is uncommented. It also makes no difference if column "v" has data type "text".
